title: Advanced Propulsion Centre (APC): impact evaluation
file_title: Advanced Propulsion Centre impact evaluation: final report
description: The APC provides public support for late-stage R&D and manufacturing process innovation research projects and aims to achieve significant progress in developing low carbon and zero emission vehicle propulsion technologies, anchor and attract research and development and manufacturing capability to the UK, and leverage high value manufacturing opportunities that market exploitation may provide.
findings: This independent evaluation final report assesses the impact of the Advanced Propulsion Centre (APC) core competition for automotive research and development grant funding. title: Apprenticeships and the Pay Review Body workforces: Final Report
file_title: Apprenticeships and the pay review body workforces report : August 2020
description: This document describes an evaluation of the impact of apprenticeships on recruitment and retention in various UK public sectors, including teaching, the armed forces, police, and the NHS. The evaluation, which uses expert interviews, surveys, and case studies, finds that apprenticeships have a mixed impact across sectors, with implementation challenges in some and vocational training benefits in others. The apprenticeship levy and new standards have influenced employer decisions, with varied opinions on their effectiveness. The Police Constable Degree Apprenticeship (PCDA) program, specifically, has increased police numbers and fostered a new learning culture but also brought resource allocation challenges. Overall, the document concludes that while apprenticeships have potential for workforce development, their success depends on overcoming funding, infrastructure, and training alignment issues. Further analysis is needed to fully understand their role in public sector workforce management.

title: Early insights evaluation of postmaster engagement​
description: An external evaluation of the current postmaster engagement initiatives implemented by Post Office Ltd, assessed against government priorities and objectives, and different stakeholders’ expectations and understandings of what good engagement means. Aims to generate early insights into what is and isn’t working in postmaster inclusion, and suggest how to improve or change the current approach.
findings: Awareness of engagement initiatives was mixed. Whilst postmasters were broadly positive about increased engagement activity, they felt impact was not yet visible in their branches. Many were unsure how various engagement mechanisms fit together or influenced actual decision‑making. Over half (55%) of postmasters felt government should hear directly from them. Across comparable organisations with distributed networks, effective engagement depends on a mix of variables, including clear mandated representatives, early involvement of operator expertise, and consistent communication of outcomes.

title: Office of Manpower Economics: Review of the Use and Effectiveness of Market Pay Supplements - Project Report
file_title: Review of the Use and Effectiveness of Market Pay Supplements: November 2017
description: This document describes an evaluation of market pay supplements and Recruitment and Retention Payments (RRPs) in the public sector, focusing on their effectiveness in sectors such as healthcare, IT, the Armed Forces, and local government, with a particular emphasis on nurses, IT workers, and social workers. The Institute for Employment Studies (IES) conducted the evaluation using a mixed-method approach that included stakeholder interviews, case studies, and a rapid evidence review. The findings reveal that the success of these financial incentives is variable and context-dependent, influenced by factors like skill shortages and employee involvement in pay policies. While financial incentives can aid recruitment, the study suggests that a combination of financial and non-financial incentives, tailored to specific situations and supported by a comprehensive HR strategy, may be more effective. The importance of clear objectives, transparent criteria, and regular monitoring of these incentives is emphasized, along with the involvement of employee representatives in designing pay schemes. The evaluation recommends a total reward approach and highlights the need for regular governance to ensure the effectiveness and appropriate use of RRPs.

title: Tranche 1: Findings from the Regulatory Horizons Council evaluation interviews and retrospective
file_title: Tranche 1: Findings from the Regulatory Horizons Council evaluation interviews and retrospective (PDF)
description: This document describes the evaluation of the Regulatory Horizons Council's (RHC) first set of deep dives, focusing on the regulation of drones and other technologies. The RHC, praised for its independence and effective stakeholder management, aims to provide neutral and credible reports to drive regulatory issues forward. The evaluation was conducted through 14 one-hour interviews with key stakeholders, structured to allow probing questions, and complemented by retrospective workshops. Results indicated that while the RHC's reports were insightful and stimulated thinking, there were challenges such as resourcing issues due to COVID-19, confusion about the RHC's role, and difficulties in stakeholder buy-in. The evaluation found that improvements are needed in timing, collaboration, direct stakeholder involvement, and follow-up on reports. Future actions for the RHC include maintaining process flexibility, nurturing a supportive environment, improving information management, and building technical expertise. The RHC is also revising its communication strategy and developing new approaches for engagement post-publication.
